locator: VII, lect. 2 n. 892: both the mover and the mobile are being moved simultaneously
interpretation: When something moves by virtue of being moved by another, mover and moved are moved at the same time, as the hand and the stick; so all the motions of the hypothesized chain exist together. Read as the same proposition as Aristotle's claim ARIST-PHYS-242A20-CHAIN-SIMULTANEOUS-A. It shows that the series Aquinas considers is one of present, simultaneous moved movers (the hand-and-stick model), the per se series of ST I q.2 a.3 and I q.46 a.2 ad 7. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
